clue.text: Political disaster with sailor hat?

parts.note: a tar is an old slang word for a sailor
a jokey reference to George W. Bush, the US president, cast as a political disaster

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sailor's hat was a political disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarbush (tarboosh) is a fez-like cap; the surface's political disaster is a dig at President Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarbush is a brimless felt cap like a fez, worn in the Middle East, so it is a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Dum or Dee used to wash

definitions.text: Dum or Dee used to wash

parts.words: Dum or Dee used to wash
parts.note: Tweedledum and Tweedledee are tubby twins; the phrase is also an old washing machine with two drums

explanation.surface: One of Lewis Carroll's rotund twins is put to use doing the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: A twin tub is a British washing machine with separate washing and spinning drums; Carroll's Tweedle brothers are fat identical twins.
explanation.definitionFit: A washing machine with two separate drums, one for washing and one for spinning, popular in older British homes.

clue.text: Plan for land corps?

parts.note: rearranging the letters of crops, a rotation of them, gives the clue word corps

explanation.surface: A question about a strategy for land forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land corps' suggests an army; but the answer read as wordplay, a rotation of the letters of CROPS, spells CORPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crop rotation is a farming scheme for using fields in turn, so it is a plan for managing land.

clue.text: Angular, not like Dum or Dee

definitions.meaning: having corners or sharp angles, not curved
Tweedledum and Tweedledee are famously round and plump, so anything not like them is not round

explanation.surface: Someone bony and angular, quite unlike Carroll's plump twins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without curves or roundness is angular, and the plump Tweedle twins are the opposite of that shape.

clue.text: Pipe and a book

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

explanation.surface: A list of two items: a pipe and a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is a book of the Old Testament, named for one of the minor prophets.

clue.text: Predators take constant levies

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant for a circle's ratio
rates are local taxes or levies

explanation.surface: Greedy predators keep collecting the same charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates prey on shipping, robbing vessels at sea, so they are predators in a human sense.

clue.text: ''Gordius'' as maybe used on my first puzzle

indicators.note: the first letter of the word puzzle is taken
maybe suggests the letters of the words used on my are not fixed but could be rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter recalls the name he signed on his earliest crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal; 'first' picks the opening letter of 'puzzle'. Gordius is this setter's own byline, the clue's in-joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordius is a setter's assumed name, so it is an example of a pen name used instead of a real one.

clue.text: Abbreviated prayer taking on at cathedral

parts.note: RIP abbreviates requiescat in pace, rest in peace, a prayer for the dead
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shortened prayer is said at a cathedral service.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire, England, so it stands for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon in North Yorkshire is known for its cathedral, so the place name stands for one.

clue.text: Causes of some parental explosions?

parts.note: end-of-term school assessments can make parents furious; terminal also hints at devices that set off explosions

explanation.surface: What makes some parents blow up?
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the school year has three terms, each ending with a written assessment sent home to parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Written school assessments sent home at the end of a term often cause parental anger.

clue.text: Spot by a tricky investigative craft

indicators.note: tricky suggests something intricate and twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spotting a sneaky vessel used for snooping.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat used for spying gathers intelligence, so it is a vessel used for investigation.

clue.text: One not apathetic enough to vote?

definitions.text: One not apathetic enough to vote?

parts.words: One not apathetic enough to vote?
parts.note: a person with a stake in the matter; read playfully, someone keen on a political faction who will bother to vote

explanation.surface: A question about who cares enough to go to the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a stake in an outcome is concerned, the opposite of apathetic, and here punningly keen on a political group.

clue.text: Edentate taking a turn from actress, Audrey

indicators.note: taking ... from means the following letters are removed from the actress's surname

parts.note: Audrey Tautou is the French actress who starred in Amelie
a U-turn, so a turn is the letter U

explanation.surface: An animal without teeth borrows a turn from the French actress Audrey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... from' removes U (a U-turn) from TAUTOU, leaving TATOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The tatou is an armadillo, and armadillos belong to the order Edentata, mammals lacking front teeth.

clue.text: Movement or part also not in a movement

parts.note: and means also, in addition

indicators.note: movement signals the letters of not in a are moved about

explanation.surface: A section of a symphony is described as being out of motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' appears twice: first as the musical sense in the definition, then as the anagram signal turning NOTINA into ANTINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking, slightly faster than andante, giving its name to a movement or section of a work.

clue.text: Derisive expression at second class ring road works

parts.note: B is the grade for second class

indicators.note: works suggests roadworks and things being reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mocking look at a second-rate ring road under construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' turns RINGROAD into ROADGRIN; a ring road is a British bypass circling a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide smile can be mocking or scornful, so it is a derisive expression on the face.

clue.text: File short garbled report

indicators.note: garbled means mixed up, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A journalist files a muddled, brief report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a news story; it is the bang of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp noise of a gun firing, and the shot of a rifle makes one.

clue.text: Treaty of Rome? It refers to the moon!

parts.note: the Treaty of Rome founded the European Economic Community, so it suggests E for European
a pact is a treaty or agreement

explanation.surface: A question about the Treaty of Rome, with an unexpected link to the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Treaty of Rome (1957) set up the European Economic Community, so it was a European pact: E plus PACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An epact is the moon's age on 1 January, used in calculating the date of Easter, so the term concerns lunar time.

clue.text: Spectacular leap in begging not unknown outside church

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps round the other
not removes the unknown letter from the word for begging

parts.note: an entreaty is an act of begging
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A dramatic jump made while pleading outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the algebraic unknown from the begging word, and 'outside' makes what remains wrap the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrechat is a ballet jump in which the dancer crosses the legs repeatedly in mid-air.

clue.text: Anxiously consider the children

definitions.meaning: to worry over something at length, dwelling on it
a family's young, as a litter or clutch of offspring

explanation.surface: A parent worrying over the children.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to dwell on a worry, and a brood is a set of young offspring in a family.

clue.text: Number from Labour turned Tory with fateful declaration

indicators.note: turned means the short form of Labour is turned backwards

parts.note: Lab is the usual abbreviation for the British Labour Party
four is a number

explanation.surface: A politician who defected from Labour to the Conservatives made a fateful statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Balfour, Conservative prime minister, issued the 1917 Balfour Declaration on Palestine. 'turned' reverses LAB; 'Number' hints at Number 10, but here gives FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was a Conservative statesman whose 1917 declaration backed a Jewish homeland in Palestine.

clue.text: Trauma of one upset by smoking here

definitions.note: plural rooms are meant, places where smoking happens

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Smoking is blamed for upsetting someone after a trauma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TRAUMAOF plus I (one) into FUMATORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumatoria are rooms set aside for smoking, the plural of the Latin-derived fumatorium.

clue.text: Article to cover an actress

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to dress is to clothe or cover

explanation.surface: An article is written to cover a film actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Ursula Andress is the Swiss actress of the first James Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursula Andress is a Swiss film actress famous for an early James Bond film.

clue.text: See disturbed child life

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A troubled childhood is observed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a bishop's diocese. Lichfield is a cathedral city in Staffordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lichfield is the seat of a bishop, and a bishop's area of authority is called a see.

clue.text: Charges said to perturb

indicators.note: said means the word is heard as spoken

parts.note: fees are charges for a service

explanation.surface: Hearing about the charges is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: Feeze is an old dialect word meaning to worry or bother.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeze is a dialect verb meaning to fret or agitate, so it matches a word for disturbing someone.

clue.text: Indian hemp reported as possible cause of bodily harm

indicators.note: reported as means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a dagger can inflict a stab wound

explanation.surface: Cannabis is reported as a possible cause of physical injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Dagga is the South African name for cannabis; in non-rhotic British speech it sounds like DAGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagga is cannabis, the plant also called Indian hemp, smoked as a drug in southern Africa.

clue.text: Antiseptic used in Brussels apartment

parts.note: the European Union has its headquarters in Brussels, so the city stands for EU
a pad is slang for a flat or apartment

explanation.surface: An antiseptic is used in a flat in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: Eupad is a dated antiseptic powder made of bleaching powder and boric acid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eupad was a chlorine-based antiseptic powder used on wounds, especially in the First World War.

clue.text: Adopting an attitude of a master of hounds

definitions.meaning: behaving in a haughty, superior way
literally describing a hunt master, seated up on a tall mount

explanation.surface: A hunt master striking a superior pose.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting arrogant and self-righteous, and literally fits a mounted hunt master.

clue.text: Buzz word of government engineers with no children getting shock treatment

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
s.p. abbreviates sine prole, the genealogists' term for dying without issue
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a shock treatment

explanation.surface: A government slogan involves childless engineers receiving electric shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Respect agenda' was a Blair government slogan of the 2000s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair's government made a slogan of this word, promoting good behaviour through its Respect agenda.

clue.text: They may be in favour of public hanging

definitions.text: They may be in favour of public hanging

parts.words: They may be in favour of public hanging
parts.note: painters like their work hung on gallery walls for the public to see, not executions

explanation.surface: Supporters of public executions.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters want their pictures displayed on gallery walls, which is a public hanging of art.
